quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #16
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: When a school bus stops ahead to pick up or drop off children, you must:

options.text: Stop completely until all children have left the bus.
Stop completely until the red lights stop flashing and the stop arm goes up.
Change lanes, drive slowly, and pass the bus carefully.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely until the red lights stop flashing and the stop arm goes up.
questions.explanation: When a school bus stops with flashing red lights and its stop arm out, you must stop completely. Do not move until the lights stop flashing and the stop arm is raised. Even after the bus starts moving, check that no children are crossing the road before you proceed.

questions.question: Which factor affects how fast a person absorbs alcohol?

options.text: Weight
Height
Intelligence

questions.correctAnswerText: Weight
questions.explanation: A person's weight affects how fast they absorb alcohol. Other factors include biological sex and how much food is in their stomach. The only way to remove alcohol from your body is to wait for time to pass.

questions.question: If you park your vehicle in an unusual parking area, you must:

options.text: Park with your reverse lights on.
Make sure other drivers can see your vehicle from all directions.
Park five feet away from the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure other drivers can see your vehicle from all directions.
questions.explanation: You must make sure your parked vehicle does not become a hazard. No matter where you park, make sure drivers approaching from any direction can see your car clearly.

questions.question: At an intersection with a flashing red traffic light, you must:

options.text: Stop completely, give way to traffic and pedestrians, then go.
Slow down and go forward carefully.
Stop completely and stay stopped while the light is red.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely, give way to traffic and pedestrians, then go.
questions.explanation: Treat a flashing red light like a stop sign. Stop completely, give way to oncoming traffic and pedestrians, and only go when it is safe.

questions.question: If pedestrians are crossing in the middle of the street instead of at a crosswalk, you:

options.text: Must stop for them.
Do not have to stop for them.
Should honk your horn at them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Must stop for them.
questions.explanation: You must give way to pedestrians at all times, even if they are crossing illegally. Always stop for pedestrians, regardless of where they are crossing.

questions.question: If you are under 21, your license can be suspended if you drive with a blood alcohol level of:

options.text: 0.15 percent or higher.
0.08 percent or higher.
Any amount.

questions.correctAnswerText: Any amount.
questions.explanation: Drivers under 21 have zero tolerance for alcohol. If any alcohol is found in your system, you face serious penalties, including a two-year license suspension.

questions.question: When can you drive on the shoulder of the road?

options.text: Only when an official tells you to.
When the car in front is driving too slowly.
When the car in front is turning.

questions.correctAnswerText: Only when an official tells you to.
questions.explanation: You can only drive on the shoulder when a police officer or other official directs you to do so. Do not use the shoulder to pass other vehicles.

questions.question: Which of these slows down traffic flow?

options.text: Slowing down to look at a collision.
Avoiding unnecessary lane changes.
Using public transportation instead of driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slowing down to look at a collision.
questions.explanation: Looking at collisions or unusual events (called rubbernecking) slows traffic and causes congestion. Avoid doing this.

questions.question: Which statement about changing lanes is correct?

options.text: You only need to look over your right shoulder for any lane change.
Look over your right shoulder for a right lane change and your left shoulder for a left lane change.
Cars with two outside mirrors have no blind spots.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look over your right shoulder for a right lane change and your left shoulder for a left lane change.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, signal and check your mirrors. Look over your shoulder to check your blind spot and make sure no vehicles, motorcycles, or bicycles are in the next lane.

questions.question: When can you block an intersection?

options.text: If you entered on a green light.
During rush hour traffic.
Never.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never.
questions.explanation: Do not enter an intersection unless you can completely cross it before the light turns red. Even with a green light, blocking the intersection is illegal and you can receive a citation.

questions.question: If the road ahead is flooded, what should you do?

options.text: Slam on the brakes.
Do not drive through the flood. Turn around and take another route.
Drive only in the center of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not drive through the flood. Turn around and take another route.
questions.explanation: Never drive on a flooded road. Water may hide danger, even if it looks shallow. Turn around and find a different way to your destination.

questions.question: After passing a vehicle, when is it safe to move back into the right lane?

options.text: After about three seconds.
When you can no longer see the other vehicle in your right mirror.
When you can see the entire front of the other vehicle in your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you can see the entire front of the other vehicle in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: After passing, return to your lane only when you can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror. Always check your blind spots before moving back.

questions.question: Which lane should you be in to make a left turn from a one-way street?

options.text: The lane closest to the left curb.
The lane closest to the center of the street.
The lane closest to the right curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: The lane closest to the left curb.
questions.explanation: When turning, use the lane closest to the direction you want to turn. For a left turn from a one-way street, be in the lane nearest the left curb.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Do not enter.
Yield the right-of-way.
Reserved parking for people with disabilities.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not enter.
questions.explanation: This sign is posted on one-way streets and other roads where you cannot enter. You may see it when trying to enter an expressway ramp in the wrong direction.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Bicycle crossing.
Stop only if other cars are approaching.
Yield the right-of-way to pedestrians.

questions.correctAnswerText: Bicycle crossing.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are usually yellow with black markings. They alert drivers that bicycles may be crossing the road.

questions.question: How do you check your blind spots?

options.text: By looking in your side mirrors.
By turning your head and looking over your shoulders.
By looking in your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: By turning your head and looking over your shoulders.
questions.explanation: Blind spots are areas you cannot see in your mirrors. Check them by turning your head and looking over your shoulders.

questions.question: When passing another car, when do you have enough space to return to your lane?

options.text: If the other driver signals for you to return.
If you look over your shoulder and see the passed car behind you.
If you can see both of the passed vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: If you can see both of the passed vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Make sure there is safe distance between your vehicle and the passed vehicle before returning to your lane. When you can see both headlights in your rearview mirror, it is safe to move back.

questions.question: When driving near a large truck, what should you do?

options.text: Follow the truck closely to reduce wind drag on your vehicle.
Avoid driving beside it for long periods of time.
Drive on its right side when on curves and hills.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid driving beside it for long periods of time.
questions.explanation: Large trucks have large blind spots on each side. Do not drive beside them for long periods of time.

questions.question: If you have a green light but the intersection is blocked by traffic, what should you do?

options.text: Turn left and find another route.
Stay out of the intersection until traffic clears.
Follow the other vehicles and enter the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay out of the intersection until traffic clears.
questions.explanation: Do not enter the intersection even if your light is green if traffic is blocking your way. If you enter and the light changes, you will block cross traffic and may get a ticket.

questions.question: If your vehicle loses traction on wet road, what should you do?

options.text: Drive at a constant speed to gain better traction.
Apply the brakes firmly to prevent sliding.
Slow down gradually without using the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down gradually without using the brakes.
questions.explanation: When driving in heavy rain, your tires may lose grip and slide on water. This is called hydroplaning. If this happens, slow down gradually and do not use the brakes.

questions.question: When entering a roundabout, you should slow down and:

options.text: Yield to pedestrians and bicyclists crossing.
Yield to cars already in the roundabout.
Both of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: When entering a roundabout, you must yield to pedestrians, bicyclists, and cars already in the roundabout.

questions.question: Which statement about blind spots is true?

options.text: Blind spots go away if you have one outside mirror on each side.
Large trucks have bigger blind spots than most cars.
You can see blind spots by looking in your rearview mirrors.

questions.correctAnswerText: Large trucks have bigger blind spots than most cars.
questions.explanation: Blind spots are areas you cannot see in your mirrors. Large trucks have large blind spots that other drivers should avoid.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: No right turn.
You must turn right.
Watch for traffic on your right.

questions.correctAnswerText: No right turn.
questions.explanation: This sign means you cannot turn right. Right turns are not allowed where this sign is posted.

questions.question: If there is a deep puddle on the road ahead, you should:

options.text: Keep the posted speed to get through the water.
Avoid the puddle if possible.
Shift into neutral while driving through the water.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid the puddle if possible.
questions.explanation: Avoid slippery areas like puddles, ice, wet leaves, and oil to prevent skidding. Dry, solid surfaces are safest for driving.

questions.question: Always stop before crossing railroad tracks when:

options.text: Your vehicle cannot completely cross the tracks before stopping.
The crossing is in a city with frequent train traffic.
You are carrying two or more young children.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your vehicle cannot completely cross the tracks before stopping.
questions.explanation: A train can come on any track at any time. Make sure your vehicle completely clears the tracks before you stop.
